review.reason: Provenance, containment, and prohibited-artifact validation are project tooling, exercised with synthetic manifests rather than reference programs.
Staging and capture integrity are properties of the recording tools. Their tests do not substitute for required language recordings.
Normalization is a project-defined byte transformation tested with fixed inputs; it does not assert new language behavior.
Trace-link and history enforcement are project validation rules tested with synthetic inventories and Git history. Inventory completeness remains a separate obligation.
Phase readiness and regression enforcement are project policies. Synthetic pending and verified cases test the rules without inventing reference observations.
Canonical AST printing, comment preservation and idempotence are project tooling contracts; recorded source/output probes separately establish language behavior.
Command dispatch, stream separation, exit statuses, and explicit work budgets are project interfaces absent from the reference editor.
Injected Go host errors and retained error causes are embedding contracts absent from the reference editor; source-level environment failures require their own recordings.
The project formatter standard-output, check and in-place modes have no corresponding reference CLI; incomplete mode and comment behavior remains pending.

Collected parser diagnostics, source and syntax-depth safeguards, and bounded adversarial processing are project contracts; reference error-discovery phases and accepted syntax remain separately required.
Public diagnostic codes, severity, wrapped Go causes, rendering, and the semantic handoff are project API contracts; reference language diagnostics remain independently recorded.
AST order, source spans and comment anchors are project data structures not exposed by the reference editor; accepted grammar remains covered by recorded programs.
The shared REPL input stream and EOF submission are project interfaces, verified with transcript and CLI tests rather than reference editor behavior.

Automatic REPL submission, prompt ordering, shared input, and recovery are project interface behavior. Transcript and CLI tests verify these paths without replacing reference evidence for the submitted language programs.
Unicode outside Windows-1252 and unpositioned reference conversion faults need explicit portable guard diagnostics; these do not establish reference diagnostic positions.

Malformed Go storage layouts cannot be injected through reference source programs. These project guards are tested with synthetic storage objects; recorded ordinary bounds failures remain separately required.
The original clock resets its hour before its outer condition can end; complete execution is excluded from the finite sweep, while timer, loop, string and display behavior remain required.
